title: Serve from Zip
content:
This page is internal and intended for IPEX DevOps Team.

Akamai Serve from Zip needs be enabled (or disabled if that is requested) on both storage group level and on upload account level. In addition, index.html need to be configured as the default document for directory (with trailing slash) in property configuration.

Enable/Disable on Storage Group Level

  1. Open the application. Go to ☰ ⇒ ORIGIN SERVICES ⇒ NetStorage.

  2. Select the Storage Groups entity.

  3. Click on Edit storage group.

  4. Under upload directories, click on Action (...) to edit the upload directory.

  5. Enable the Serve From Zip option and Save the changes.

Enable/Disable on Upload Account Level

  1. Open the application. Go to ☰ ⇒ ORIGIN SERVICES ⇒ NetStorage.

  2. Select the Upload Accounts entity.

  3. Select the upload account to edit

  4. Click Edit in the upper right corner

  5. Go down to Advanced Settings

  6. Select Append serve-from-zip index to enable serve from zip, or select Store without change (default) to disable

  7. Under upload directories, click on Action (...) to edit the upload directory.

  8. Enable the Serve From Zip option and Save the changes.

Configure index.html as default document

To get the standard behavior and serve index.html when surfing to directory (with trailing slash) as specified for NetStorage when serve form zip is not enable rewrite functionality in property configuration can be used.

Example: If you currently access your application like this: https://www.cte.ikeadt.com/addon-app/app/1.2.3/#/se/en/ then below property configuration needs to be added for application path.

Troubleshooting

“Not a sfz file.”

If this error message is returned, doublecheck the following:

  1. That the upload account has “Append serve-from-zip index” enabled

  2. That correct private SSH key is used.

For example, if two upload accounts are used for two different directory associations (two separate SSH keys) and one account has serve from zip enabled and the other not, make sure the correct key is used. Also note that if you use an SSH key that has access to multiple product directories; for example access to directories that can serve zip contents, it does not mean that this account can upload zip files to that destination, unless the upload account has serve from zip enabled.

Example: upload account “parent” has the following directory association - without serve from zip enabled:

/809385/addon-app/parent

The upload account “child” has the following association - with serve from zip enabled:

/809385/addon-app/parent/child/contents

If the GitHub workflow, or Jenkins server, uploads to /809385/addon-app/parent/child/contents but with the SSH key from the parent account, serve from zip will not work. Hence, make sure the correct SSH key is used in the pipeline.
